absent: Locking, concurrency and reference counting around module state, symbol lookup waiting and namespace handling are not shown.
Exact memory type definitions, alignment, allocation and protection of core and init regions beyond bucket mapping are not shown.
Architecture specific relocation application, per CPU allocation mechanics and livepatch payload handling beyond dispatch are not shown.
Decompression, signature enforcement and security hook decision details beyond their invocation points are not shown.
Module attribute table contents, taint flag values and version checksum comparison beyond presence and count checks are not shown.

findings.text: Weak default classifier reports whether a section name denotes loader initialization content by testing its leading characters for the init marker. It may be overridden by architecture code.
Weak default classifier reports whether a section name denotes exit content by testing its leading characters for the exit marker. It may be overridden by architecture code.

Layout routing predicate decides if a section belongs in the initialization allocation group. When unload support is absent, exit content is also routed to the initialization group; otherwise the decision defers to the init classifier.
Weak default architecture gate for module images approves every image. Architectures may override it to enforce additional header constraints during header validation.

A module load fails when any exported symbol it provides is already owned elsewhere. The loader scans the module export range and performs a global lookup in a licensing permissive mode; a hit causes rejection with ENOEXEC.
On 386 and x86 64 machine types the loader tolerates an undefined reference to the toolchain global offset table name. On other machine types no undefined name receives this tolerance.

Common symbols are rejected unless their names carry a specific compiler link time optimization prefix, with guidance to build without common linkage. Absolute symbols need no adjustment. Livepatch marked symbols are left for later resolution by livepatch logic.

Undefined symbols are resolved through a waiting resolver. Success fixes the symbol value to the resolved address. Failure is tolerated only for weak bindings or for the ignored toolchain name; otherwise the loader warns about an unknown symbol and fails with the resolver status or ENOENT.

Defined symbols must reference a section index within the header section count or the load fails. Per CPU symbols are rebased against the module per CPU area while other symbols are rebased against their section runtime address.

Relocation processing visits every section except the reserved zero entry, skips entries whose target index is out of range and skips non allocated targets except the per CPU template. Livepatch flagged sections use the livepatch applier while REL and RELA typed sections use their respective appliers; the first failure stops the walk.

Section placement follows five ordered buckets that separate executable allocated content, plain allocated read only content, read only after init content, writable allocated content, and small allocated content. Core and initialization groups map these buckets to distinct text, read only data, post init read only, and data memory types, with one initialization bucket marked invalid and skipped with a one time warning.

During layout, sections claimed by code tagging are excluded from ordinary offset assignment. Their size field is repurposed to record the intended memory type while the section stays in preallocated contiguous tagging storage.

Missing license metadata is treated as unspecified. A license that is not compatible with the general public license taints the kernel for proprietary loading with an additional reliability caveat for lock dependency tracking, warning once per previously untainted kernel.

Module namespace imports are gathered from repeated modinfo entries into a single newline separated buffer terminated by null, with no allocation when absent. Any import carrying the reserved module prefix is rejected with EPERM.

Every section carrying file contents must satisfy that its offset plus size neither wraps nor exceeds the total image length. Violations cause rejection with ENOEXEC, with width handling that covers both 32 and 64 bit builds.

An image is accepted only when its length covers an ELF header, its magic matches the ELF signature, its type denotes a relocatable object, and both the generic architecture check and the module specific architecture check approve the header. Any failure causes rejection.

Section headers are accepted only when entry size matches the native header size and the table lies fully inside the image. Section zero must be null typed with zero size and zero address. Content bearing sections must pass the offset bounds check before their table pointer is cached.

The section name table index must be defined and within range and must point at a string table. The table must be non empty and null terminated at its end, and every non null section name offset must lie inside it before the name base is cached.

At most one modinfo section may exist; duplicates cause rejection while absence allows an early success without a cached index. When present, its index is cached and the module name field is captured early for diagnostic use.

Exactly one module descriptor section with the reserved link once name must exist, must carry contents rather than uninitialized storage, must be marked for allocation during execution, and must size exactly to the running kernel module structure. Any deviation causes rejection.

Exactly one symbol table section must exist or the image is rejected as stripped. Its linked string section index must be defined and within range and must denote a string table before it is cached as the symbol string table.

When the caller suppresses module version handling, all version related indexes are cleared and treated as absent. Otherwise extended version checksum and name sections must appear together or not at all, and the count of checksum entries must match the sequence of null terminated names; mismatch causes rejection.
The symbol string table must be non empty, must begin with null and must end with null. Every symbol name offset must lie inside the table before the table base is cached for later resolution.

User supplied images are length checked before any security gate, then passed through a load permission check, copied fully into non pageable kernel storage, and passed through a post load security check naming the init module operation. Allocation failure, copy failure and security denial each abort the load with cleanup of the temporary image.
Copies from user space proceed in bounded chunks with voluntary rescheduling between chunks. Any chunk copy failure aborts the whole transfer with a fault status.

After validation, every section runtime address field is pointed at its location inside the temporary image with section zero forced to zero. Version and modinfo sections have their allocation marking cleared so they are tracked but not retained in the loaded image.

A livepatch modinfo marker requires livepatch support to accept the module as a livepatch payload or the load fails. A retpoline modinfo marker is checked for compiler mitigation approval, with a warning when the module lacks the expected mitigation.
Temporary image release distinguishes compressed from plain loads. Compressed images use a dedicated decompression cleanup path while plain images release the temporary allocation directly.

Modinfo attributes with setup handlers are initialized from their named modinfo values during setup, and attributes with teardown handlers are released during modinfo cleanup. Import namespace copying follows attribute setup and prefix validation.

Image validation proceeds as a strict pipeline from header checks to section table caching, then name table caching, then index discovery for modinfo, descriptor, symbols, strings and versions plus per CPU discovery, then symbol string table caching, and finally caching of the descriptor pointer with fallback of the diagnostic name to the on disk module name.

Layout runs in two passes after resetting every section marker to an unassigned sentinel. The core pass assigns non initialization sections to core memory types followed by an initialization pass assigning initialization sections to init memory types, each pass respecting bucket order and skipping already assigned or mismatched sections.

Observed loader state caches the image header and length, section table pointer, section name base, symbol string base, descriptor pointer, diagnostic name, and an index group recording modinfo, descriptor, symbol table, string table, version, extended checksum, extended name and per CPU section positions.
Observed module state used here includes a name, an export table with count, and a stored namespace import list. Symbol resolution also consults per CPU storage associated with the module.

Loading is fragile to duplicate exports, common linkage, unknown or out of range symbol references, duplicate modinfo sections, missing or mis sized descriptor sections, missing symbol tables, mismatched extended version tables, and reserved namespace imports; each maps to a distinct rejection status rather than best effort continuation.

Corrupt images risk out of bounds access through section offsets, name offsets and string table reads. The loader mitigates this by enforcing header length, table containment, null termination at both ends of string tables, and per symbol name containment before caching any pointer.
The user copy chunk size is sixteen pages.
The module descriptor is located by section name .gnu.linkonce.this_module and must occupy exactly one section whose size equals the kernel module structure size.
The loader maintains a denylist of two historical license offenders, driverloader and lve.
Module metadata uses section name .modinfo with keys name and import_ns and livepatch and retpoline, while namespace imports forbid prefix module: .
Version bookkeeping uses section names __versions and __version_ext_crcs and __version_ext_names.
Default section classification recognizes leading markers .init for initialization content and .exit for exit content.
The undefined name tolerated on 386 and x86 64 images is _GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_.
